title: Relative commutative extensions of multiplicative-type groups
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. An $S$-group scheme is a group object in schemes over $S$, and a homomorphism respects multiplication, identity and inverse. An $S$-group scheme is of multiplicative type of finite presentation if it is, locally for the fppf topology [def-pc-fppf-site], isomorphic to $D_U(M)=\operatorname{Spec}_U\mathcal O_U[M]$ for a finitely generated abelian group $M$, with group-algebra Hopf operations as in [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Here the relative spectrum is obtained by gluing $\operatorname{Spec}A[M]$ over affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq U$. Let $E$ be an affine commutative $S$-group scheme, where affine means that the inverse image of every affine open of $S$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and commutative means that its multiplication is unchanged by exchanging the factors. Let $p:E\to D$ be a homomorphism that is faithfully flat (flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and surjective on underlying spaces) and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $N=E\times_{D,e_D}S$ be its scheme-theoretic kernel, with the induced group structure. If $N$ and $D$ are of multiplicative type of finite presentation, then $E$ is of multiplicative type of finite presentation. No smoothness or connectedness of $E,N,D$, no reducedness of $S$, and no residue-characteristic restriction is assumed.

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(2), printed pp.299--301, commutative case, with its short exact sequence expressed by a faithfully flat locally finitely presented homomorphism and its kernel. The middle group is automatically fppf over S since p and D -> S are fppf. WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this relative multiplicative-type extension theorem.

proof.text: The assertion is local for the fppf topology by the definition of multiplicative type: compose a covering on which the assertion holds with its diagonalizing coverings. Restrict to affine opens and then successive splitting covers for $D$ and $N$; [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change] retains the first splitting under the second cover, and [lem-pc-fppf-affine-refinement] lets us work on affine charts. Thus assume $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $D=D_A(Q)$ and $N=D_A(P)$ with $P,Q$ finitely generated. The empty base has nothing to prove. Fppf covering composition is the covering axiom of [def-pc-fppf-site].

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(2), printed p.300, local reduction; Definition B.1.1, printed p.280.

proof.text: Write $E=\operatorname{Spec}C$. By [lem-sfb-subgroup-algebra-coset-presentation] with $L=0$, $A[Q]$ and $A[P]$ are finitely presented $A$-algebras. They are free over $A$ on their displayed group bases. Tensoring a module map with either algebra is a direct sum of copies of that map, so kernels and images are computed coordinatewise; the nonempty basis also detects zero modules. Thus these algebras are flat. The affine flatness dictionary [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] applies. The given locally finitely presented map $p$ makes $A[Q]\to C$ finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation]; composition [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] makes $C$ finitely presented over $A$. The affine map $A[Q]\to C$ is flat, and composition [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp] makes $C$ flat over $A$. In particular $E$ is flat of finite presentation over $A$.

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(2), printed pp.299-300, fppf hypothesis; affine finite presentation and group-algebra calculation.

proof.text: Use the system of finitely generated integer subrings $A_i\subseteq A$ of [lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine]. By [thm-pd-spreading-out], descend $E$, its multiplication, inverse, identity, $p:E\to D_A(Q)$ and the specified isomorphism $D_A(P)\simeq E\times_{D_A(Q)}S$ to one stage. For affineness choose a finite algebra presentation of $C$ and descend its finitely many coefficients, giving affine models $E_i$ from the outset. The group diagrams, commutativity, homomorphism diagrams and both inverse equations for the kernel isomorphism are finitely many equalities of arrows; the equality clause puts all of them at a common later stage. The kernel is modelled by the same fibre product, whose coordinate ring is the tensor product of [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. All schemes in these finite diagrams are finitely presented over the base: tensor a finite algebra presentation for the fibre products, using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition]. They are affine and hence qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. This verifies the limit lemma's size and qcqs hypotheses.

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(2), printed p.300, Noetherian reduction; Stacks Tags 01ZM, 01YW.

proof.text: For the model $p_i:E_i\to D_{A_i}(Q)$, local finite presentation holds: a finite set of algebra generators for $A_i[Q]$ can be expressed in the chosen finite presentation of $C_i$, so adjoining equations equating those expressions to the generators gives a finite presentation of $C_i$ over $A_i[Q]$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-flat-ring-map] to the system $A_i[Q]\to C_i$ to arrange that $p_i$ is flat, using [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-surjective] to arrange surjectivity as well. Its schemes and bases are affine qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. The kernel is still $D_{A_i}(P)$ at later stages. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], the finite-type integer base is Noetherian. It suffices to prove the assertion for these Noetherian split models: a diagonalizing fppf covering then pulls back to the original base by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change]. Rename the model's base ring $A$.

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(2), printed p.300, Noetherian reduction; Stacks Tags 04AI and 07RR, flatness and surjectivity at a stage.

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ and let $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Let $B=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be the ring of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples]; it is local with separably closed residue field $k$. It is Noetherian by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian] and faithfully flat over $R$ by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat]. Put $V=\widehat B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] and [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal], $V$ is complete Noetherian local with the same residue field $k$; it is faithfully flat over $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]. All the given group structures and kernel identifications pull back. The base-changed quotient remains fppf by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change]. Thus $E_V$ is flat of finite presentation by the argument of step 2 over $V$.

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(2), printed p.300, strictly henselian complete local reduction; the completion is taken only after the Noetherian model.

proof.text: Let $K$ be an algebraic closure of $k$. Over $K$, apply [lem-sfb-commutative-multiplicative-type-extension] to $E_K\to D_K(Q)$ with kernel $D_K(P)$. Its groups are affine of finite type, and its coordinate map is faithfully flat: $p_K$ is the base change of the fppf map $p_V$, hence flat and surjective by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change]; flatness of the ring map is the affine dictionary, and surjectivity gives faithful flatness by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat]. Consequently $E_K\simeq D_K(M)$ for some finitely generated abelian $M$. This is also a closed subgroup of a finite power of $\mathbf G_m$: choose generators of $M$, hence a surjection $\mathbf Z^t\twoheadrightarrow M$, and apply the closed-immersion clause of [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality]. Thus $E_k$ satisfies exactly the geometric multiplicative-type hypothesis of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality], which gives a splitting over a finite separable extension of $k$. Since $k$ is separably closed, [lem-pc-sepclosed-finite-sep-trivial] makes that extension trivial. Choose $j_0:D_k(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}E_k$. No perfection or smoothness of $k$-groups has been used.

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(2), printed pp.300-301, field case; existing Milne Corollary 12.22 and Theorem 12.23 supply this case.

proof.text: Write $p_kj_0:D_k(M)\to D_k(Q)$ as $D_k(a)$ for $a:Q\to M$ using [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality]. Its fppf image is all of $D_k(Q)$. The image formula therefore makes $a$ injective: otherwise $k[Q]\to k[\operatorname{im}a]$ identifies distinct basis vectors and cannot be an isomorphism. The kernel formula identifies $\ker(p_kj_0)$ with $D_k(M/a(Q))$. This kernel is the specified $D_k(P)$, so character duality gives an isomorphism $M/a(Q)\simeq P$ under which the inclusion of the kernel is $D_k(b)$ for a surjection $b:M\twoheadrightarrow P$. Hence $0\to Q\xrightarrow{a}M\xrightarrow{b}P\to0$ is exact. Put $q=D_V(a):D_V(M)\to D_V(Q)$ and $i=D_V(b):D_V(P)\hookrightarrow D_V(M)$. The same node gives that $q$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented and that its kernel is exactly $i(D_V(P))$.

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(2), printed p.300, character extension dual to the special-fibre exact sequence.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-complete-local-diagonalizable-fibre-hom-lift] to the flat finite-type $V$-group $E_V$ and $j_0$. It gives an open and closed immersion $j:D_V(M)\to E_V$. Both $j\circ i$ and the specified kernel inclusion $n:D_V(P)\to E_V$ reduce to the same map on $k$. The injectivity of the Hom restriction map in that node, now with source $D_V(P)$ and target $E_V$, proves $j\circ i=n$. Also $p_V\circ j=q$: both are maps between split diagonalizable groups, and their character homomorphisms are locally constant by [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality]. A local ring has connected spectrum, since any open containing its closed point contains a basic open $D(f)$ with $f$ a unit and hence contains the whole spectrum. Thus each locally constant character map is constant and is determined by its special fibre. The two special fibres here are $p_kj_0=D_k(a)$.

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(2), printed p.300, lift of the special fibre, compatibility with the kernel and the quotient.

proof.text: For any $V$-scheme $T$ and $x\in E_V(T)$, the fppf cover obtained by pulling back $q$ along $p_V(x)$ has a section $y$ of $D_V(M)$ with $q(y)=p_V(x)$. On that cover $xj(y)^{-1}$ lies in $\ker p_V=N_V$, hence equals $n(z)=j(i(z))$ for a unique $z\in D_V(P)$. Therefore $x=j(i(z)y)$ fppf-locally. The cover is surjective, so applying this to points shows that every point of $E_V$ lies in the image of $j$. Since $j$ is an open immersion, its image is an open subscheme isomorphic to its source; surjectivity says this open subscheme is all of $E_V$. Thus $j$ is an isomorphism and $E_V=D_V(M)$. This step uses the fppf quotient supplied in step 7, not an assumption that every open subgroup containing the special fibre is the whole group.

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(2), printed p.300, the chain of inclusions after passage to quotients; explicit local lifting argument.

proof.text: The affine faithfully flat maps $\operatorname{Spec}V\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ are singleton fpqc covers. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] give flatness and surjectivity; over any affine open $W$ of the target, its inverse image is the fibre product of $W$ with an affine scheme over an affine scheme, hence affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], and by surjectivity its image is all of $W$; so they satisfy [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Apply [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-fpqc-descent] first to $E_B$, then to $E_R$. Their affineness and finite presentation follow by tensoring their finite algebra presentations, and their flatness follows from the quotient and the free group algebra exactly as in step 2. We conclude that $E_R$ is of multiplicative type for each prime $\mathfrak p$ of the Noetherian model $A$.

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(1),(2), printed pp.299-300, descent from the completion.

proof.text: Spread this conclusion from $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$ to a neighborhood of $\mathfrak p$ as follows. By [lem-pc-fppf-affine-refinement], choose finitely many affine charts $T_l\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ of a diagonalizing cover, with $E_{T_l}\simeq D_{T_l}(M_l)$. Each chart's algebra is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation]. The ring $R$ is the directed colimit of $A_f$, $f\notin\mathfrak p$. Descend these finite algebra presentations to some $A_f$ and descend the group isomorphisms, their inverses and their group diagrams by [thm-pd-spreading-out], using its equality clause for both inverse identities. The sources are affine fp schemes, hence qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-flat-ring-map] to make each of the finitely many chart maps flat at a common later stage. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-family-joint-surjectivity-stage] to make the chart family jointly surjective there. All its maps are lfp because the chart algebras are finitely presented. This is a diagonalizing fppf cover of $\operatorname{Spec}A_f$, with $f\notin\mathfrak p$. Thus the neighborhoods so obtained cover $\operatorname{Spec}A$, proving the assertion for the Noetherian model.

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(2), printed p.300, spreading from local rings; Stacks Tags 01ZM, 04AI and 07RR, with the cover and its surjectivity retained.

proof.text: Pull the resulting diagonalizing coverings back from the model of steps 3-4 to the original split affine base, using [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change]. Then compose with the splitting and affine-refinement covers of step 1. The fppf covering axiom [def-pc-fppf-site] gives a cover of the original $S$ on which $E$ is $D(M)$ with $M$ finitely generated. This is precisely the asserted multiplicative type of finite presentation. For the finite-presentation terminology, the group algebras are finitely presented by step 2; local finite presentation descends across fppf covers by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc] and [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-locally-finite-presentation]. An affine morphism which is lfp is of finite presentation: on affine opens of the base it is a map of affine schemes with a finite algebra presentation. This proves every claimed case without adding a smoothness, reducedness, connectedness or characteristic assumption.

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(2), printed pp.299-301, completion of the relative commutative case.
